description: Construction of single storey dwelling house to be used as a home in multiple occupation (HMO) for 4 people.
decision_conditions: Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no fencing, walls, or other means of enclosure shall be erected around the terrace areas serving the four bedrooms, as indicated on drawing no.201 , without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of residential and visual amenity, and ensuring communal living as expected for HMO development.

Prior to first occupation, a detailed Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Submitted details will demonstrate the maximum achievable energy efficiency achievable for the development and shall provide for the maximum achievable improvements in the total CO2 emissions arising from the operation of a development and its services over part L of Building Regs 2013. The Energy Statement should outline how the reductions are achieved through the use of Fabric Energy Efficiency performance, energy efficient fittings, and the use of renewable technologies. In line with Policy DMD49, the CO2 savings of the proposal shall not be less than 35%.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development must achieve reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to result in consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Core Policy 21 of the Core Strategy and the London Plan.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Biodiversity NoteDesign & Access StatementFRA20275.1HMO Use/Management NoteRefuse & Recycling StrategyPlanning Statement Energy StatementTransportation Note000201202203204205206Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation hereby approved shall be occupied by a maximum of 4 people at any one time acting as a single household and shall not be subdivided or occupied as self-contained units. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

The development hereby permitted shall be used only as a House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4) and for no other purpose, including any other use within Class C3 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking or re-enacting that Order, notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification).Reason: To ensure that the accommodation is retained in a form that provides an acceptable standard of living for occupiers and to ensure compliance with the Nationally Described Space Standards, in the interests of residential amenity.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details of 4 independently accessed long-stay cycle parking spaces have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority[KP3.1]. These details must demonstrate:Location: within the frontage of the property  Design: Stands or wall bars Security: Secure, overlooked, well-lit Coverage: Covered where possible Accessibility: Step-free, no obstructions The cycle parking spaces shall be fully constructed in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans[KP4.1], the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

The surfacing materials, for the paved area hereby approved as indicated on drawing ref-201, shall be constructed using permeable paving or other sustainable drainage systems (SUDS) that allow surface water to drain into the ground. The permeable paving shall be retained thereafter and maintained in good working order to ensure continued permeability and effective drainage[KP5.1]. Reason: To reduce surface water runoff and promote sustainable drainage in accordance with Enfield DMD Policy 45 section 3.

The privacy screen/glass balustrade on the first-floor terrace of No.27 Brimsdown Avenue shall be built in obscured glass / accordance with plan Nos. 205. The privacy glass shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining and neighbouring properties.

The parking area(s) forming part of the development shall only be used for the parking of private motor vehicles and shall not be used for any other purpose.Reason: To ensure that the development complies with Development Plan Policies and to prevent the introduction of activity which would be detrimental to amenity.
